note: Written-answer review ledger. 20.note: STEM DEFECT, and a whole damage class. The stem read 'a taxable income of 22 680' and 'he paid 000 per month in PAYG tax' -- the leading '$1' and '$3' had been eaten. In JavaScript, String.replace() treats $1..$9 in the REPLACEMENT string as capture-group references, so '$122 680' becomes '22 680' and '$3000' becomes '000'. The question was unanswerable as printed. Restored from the paper (2020 p16: 'a taxable income of $122 680 ... he paid $3000 per month'), which also matches NESA's own working (20 797 + 0.37(122 680 - 90 000) = $32 888.60; 3000 x 12 = $36 000; refund $3111.40). A sweep for the same signature across all five subjects found exactly one other instance, 2021 Q40.
